Samira / Diego — adding a few concrete items for your engineers. I kept snippets minimal so you can drop them into your repo. If you want, we can convert into a Terraform-friendly template.

1) SDK setup (examples)
- JS (node): yarn add @redwood/inference-sdk
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
  const client = new Redwood.Client({ baseUrl: 'https://api.redwood.ai', auth: { type: 'oidc', issuer: 'https://auth.astoria.com' /* OR apiKey */ } });

- Python: pip install redwood-inference
  from redwood import Client
  client = Client(base_url='https://api.redwood.ai', auth={'type':'apiKey','key':os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY')})

Recommendation: prefer OIDC for long-lived production (fine-grained scopes) and API keys for early POC/automation. OIDC reduces secrets sprawl and maps nicely to your existing IdP.

2) Model routing / policy (high-level behavior)
- Goal: serve low-latency queries from US-EAST with model A (latency-optimized), fall back to model B (cost-optimized quantized variant) when queue depth or cost thresholds hit. Also prefer regional routing for PHI-handling requests to remain in us-east-1.

Example policy (pseudocode snippet for your config file):

# routing policy: astoria-lowlatency-first
priority_rules:
  - match: region == 'us-east-1' and request.qlt == 'interactive'
    route_to: model-llm-a-lowlatency
    conditions:
      - queue_depth < 50
      - avg_90p_latency < 120ms
  - match: true
    route_to: model-llm-b-quantized
    conditions:
      - time_of_day in business-hours or burst-window

Fallback chain: primary -> regional-cost-variant -> global-cheap-fallback. The runtime supports automatic fallback with request tagging so you can track which fallback was used for reranking/telemetry.

3) Structured output + tool calling
- We recommend using the Redwood function-calling scaffold for structured actions (e.g., "create_search_query") so your frontend can safely parse results. Example: provide a function schema that returns {query: string, filters: []}. Use streaming for low-latency token-by-token UI.

4) Embeddings + re-rank flow (recommended)
- Ingest: generate 1024-dim dense vectors (or 768 if you want smaller size) and store in Vespa with a nightly reindex cadence for doc updates.
- Query-time flow: 1) client calls embeddings endpoint to vectorize the query 2) Vespa returns top-K candidates 3) call Redwood re-ranker model (structured output) to score and return final ordering.
- If you want lower TCO, keep re-ranker small and use cached candidate scores for frequent queries.

5) Auth & compliance notes
- For PHI-sensitive endpoints, pin routing to private deployment in your VPC (we can provide a Private deployment plan).
- Audit logs: we can provide token-level tracing and per-request audit IDs for any call routed through Dedicated or Private.

I’ll attach the sample config MD and a one-pager with the policy visualization.
